ideas.title: Add YouTube's 'three categories' to Israa's story review, and check that Storygraphics videos differ from each other
ideas.problem: On July 16, 2026 YouTube clarified what it will not monetise (TechCrunch, B; the Help page 'Generic or repetitive content', A): (1) mass-produced template videos with little variation, (2) content built to distress or manipulate viewers for views, (3) AI personas on finance, legal or health. YouTube says it is not a new rule, and judges the whole channel. Storygraphics (project 5) is our most exposed channel: one cast rig, one voice, one story_v1 shape, and survival/disaster stories. In quality.py, STORY_TASK criterion 10 compares only against 'earlier episodes' for copying, and criterion 11 lists gore, sex, drugs, killers, advice and politics. Neither names template sameness across our own videos or 'distress for views'. The 2026-10-04-1 sameness check was written for Shorts (shorts.py checklist), not story_v1 scripts.
ideas.proposal: 1) In quality.py STORY_TASK, replace criterion 11 with: '11. Platform risk. Advertiser-safe (no graphic gore, no sexual content, no drug instructions, no glorifying a killer, no medical, legal or financial advice, no party politics). Also answer these three YouTube monetisation tests with yes/no and one line each: (a) TEMPLATE: if you swap the names and places, is this the same cold open, same section order and same ending as the earlier episodes below? Name the shared beats. (b) DISTRESS: is suffering used as the hook instead of the story (opening on injury or fear with no other reason)? (c) SENSITIVE ADVICE: does the narrator give health, legal or money advice? Any yes on (a) or (b) means verdict rework, with the exact change.' 2) Free code check next to pre_review for story_v1: compare the new script's section headings, `shape`, first 3 words of cold_open and last sentence with earlier episodes of the same project; warn when two or more match. 3) Log the three answers on the episode (data.checks) so the owner can see them.
ideas.gain: Closes a gap between YouTube's stated rules and our checklist for the channel the owner now cares most about. Costs one more paragraph in an existing Israa call, no new run. Measure: after 3 episodes, every review carries the three answers, and at least one rework or note comes from them if the episodes are truly alike.
ideas.test: Case 1 (normal): Juliane script (ep 32) reviewed: expect (a) no, (b) no, because the story opens on a moment and has a turn. Case 2 (edge): a second survival script that copies the same shape 'countdown', the same 'Day N' markers and the same closing line: expect (a) yes with the shared beats named and verdict rework. Case 3 (failure): a script that opens with a screaming injury for 20 seconds before any context: expect (b) yes and rework. A pass is Israa returning all three answers on each of the three scripts and the verdicts above. Free test: HQ_SIMULATE=1 only checks the schema; the real test is one Israa run per script.
ideas.confidence_why: YouTube Help page (A) supports the template wording; the three categories and 'overall channel' come from TechCrunch and trade sites quoting the same interview (B), so it is one source. Weakest link: I found no official page that lists the three categories, and no data on how often template channels with recurring characters are hit.
ideas.risks: Israa may over-flag (every story has a hook and a clock). Keep the verdict rule narrow: two or more matching beats for (a). Adds a few hundred prompt tokens per review. The prompt is a rule target only if STORY_TASK is in rules.PROMPT_TARGET; otherwise this is a code edit by the Builder. Do not use it as a reason to block a script whose only fault is a similar shape; the owner decides.
